MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC WORKS COMMISSION AND PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  JOINT SPECIAL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 23, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  3:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost called the meeting to order at 3:34 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Public Works Commission (PWC) Chair Lance Simmens; Public Works
  Commission Vice Chair Wade Major; and Commissioners Scott Dittrich, Brian Merrick;
  and James Palmer; and Public Safety Commission (PSC) Chair Chris Frost; Vice Chair
  Doug Stewart; Commissioners Daphne Anneet, Keegan Gibbs, and Joshua Spiegel; and Ex
  Officio Member Brent Woodworth

  ALSO PRESENT:  Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Troy Spayd, Assistant Public
  Works Director; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Mary Linden, Executive Assistant; and
  Brandie Ayala, Senior Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Public Works Commissioner Merrick led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Senior Administrative Assistant Ayala reported that the agenda properly was posted on
  February 17, 2022 and the amended agenda posted on February 18, 2022.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Public Works Commissioner Palmer moved and Public Works Commissioner
  Dittrich seconded a motion to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the
  motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Stewart moved and Public Works
  Commissioner Palmer seconded a motion to approve the Consent Calendar. The
  question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes January 20, 2022
  —

  Recommended Action: Approve minutes for the Public Works Commission
  and Public Safety Commission Special meeting of January 20, 2022.

ITEM 1  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Westward Beach Improvements Project Update (continued from January 20, 2022)
  Recommended Action: 1) Receive an update on the Westward Beach
  Improvements Project; and 2) Provide a recommendation to City Council on any
  design modifications.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the report. He presented illustrations
  displaying details of the alternative project options.

  Lonnie Gordon stated the items had changed since she first saw the plan. She
  expressed her objection to building a wall. She expressed support for a wooden
  boardwalk on the beach side. She discussed concerns about tides and the need for
  a tide study. She stated she would support abandoning the project now and
  reconsidering it later.

  Philippe Browning stated the project originated in 2016 over concerns for public
  safety, but there were no studies to prove that issue. He proposed not extending
  concrete or timbers over an area susceptible to king tides. He stated pedestrians
  could walk on the beach. He suggested adding traffic management coordinated
  between all agencies. He stated he would appeal the project to the California
  Coastal Commission (CCC) again if appropriate studies were not done.

  Ryan Embree discussed public safety benefits of angled parking. He suggested
  angled parking be reconsidered but only on the beach side.

  Sam Hall Kaplan discussed the no-construction concept he submitted by email. He
  stated the concept was based on living streets and was experience-oriented toward
  pedestrians.

  Kraig Hill stated a wave uprush study had to be done to determine what was
  possible. He suggested rehabbing the asphalt and potentially dedicating space on
  the beach side for pedestrian or bike traffic. He stated the most important
  component was traffic control. He stated any boardwalk should be biodegradable.
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of February 23, 2022

  In response to Public Safety Commissioner Anneet, Public Works Director
  DuBoux clarified the location of the City’s right-of-way. Public Safety
  Commissioner Anneet asked what goals were driving this project. She expressed
  interest in the concept proposed by Mr. Kaplan. She stated it would provide a safe
  place for people to congregate.

  In response to Public Works Commissioner Dittrich, Public Works Director
  DuBoux discussed a roll-up sidewalk. He stated he was discussing with Los
  Angeles County Beaches and Harbors (B&H) the possibility of an ADA ramp
  surface that could provide accessibility to the beach and the water. In response to
  Public Safety Commissioner Anneet, he stated public safety concerns about
  pedestrians walking in the road and emergency vehicle access were the main
  reasons for the project. He stated requiring payment for parking may be necessary.
  He expressed support for prohibiting parking of recreational vehicles (RV). He
  suggested repaving with designated parallel parking spots on both sides. He stated
  Sunset Restaurant needed to be restricted to parking only its own lot.

  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Stewart suggested moving parallel parking
  currently east of the lifeguard stand as displayed in Option 2 to the land side. He
  stated it would provide 15 feet for pedestrian and bike pathways.

  Public Works Commissioner Palmer thanked the Commissioners for well thought-
  out options for this project. He agreed a wave uprush study and sea level rise study
  needed to be completed first. He suggested all City Commissions read the City’s
  Mission Statement at the opening of meetings.

  Public Works Commissioner Merrick stated many comments misunderstood that
  the project would be adding parking. He stated CCC would not allow elimination
  of any parking, as suggested by Mr. Kaplan and Public Safety Commission Vice
  Chair Stewart. He suggested rehabbing the asphalt to its original width. He
  displayed photos of degraded asphalt, the original edge of pavement currently under
  sand, pedestrians walking on the roadway, and a modular walkway system for
  wheelchair beach access. He suggested staying within the original width, laying
  down a boardwalk, and installing speed humps and a stop sign at the crossover
  creek area, if possible, with a flip sign to indicate ‘parking lot full.’ He agreed with
  Public Works Commissioner Dittrich that traffic control and emergency ingress and
  egress were the primary goals to be addressed.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost stated boardwalks laid down on the beach
  were common in Florida.

  Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs agreed with Public Works Commissioner
  Merrick’ s points. He stated extending concrete to the original width was the most
  efficient way to provide additional safe pedestrian walkways. He stated the western
  portion of Westward Beach Road had significant road erosion, including a drop-off
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of February 23, 2022
Page4ofl2

  to the dry sand that would require significant engineering. In response to Public
  Safety Commissioner Gibbs, Public Works Director DuBoux stated a parallel
  parking space would extend 20 feet. He stated perpendicular parking required
  greater space for the turning radius. He stated moving all the parking to the land
  side could not accommodate the current number of parking spaces. Public Safety
  Commissioner Gibbs expressed support for a rebuild of the original road width and
  a gap for pedestrians.

  Public Works Commission Chair Simmens asked if walkways on both sides
  included bike lanes within them. Public Works Director DuBoux stated most
  cyclists would continue to ride in the roadway. He stated the original plan
  accommodated bike lanes. Public Works Commission Chair Simmens expressed
  disappointment for losing bike lanes.

  Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs stated the slower traffic on Westward Beach
  Road allowed cyclists to ride on the roadway more safely.

  Public Works Commission Chair Simmens discussed concerns about cyclists
  running into opening car doors. He agreed with Public Works Commissioner
  Merrick’s suggestion for more slightly angled parking spaces. He expressed interest
  in Mr. Kaplan’s concept as a balance of safety and environmental. He stated the
  loss of the cycling aspect is troubling. He stated cycling should be promoted.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost discussed when the CCC previously
  required the City to add new parking spaces in areas near where other spaces were
  removed. He agreed with Public Works Commission Chair Simmens about the
  value of bike paths.

  Public Safety Commission Ex Officio Member Woodworth suggested curbing
  could prevent sand from getting on the road. He agreed with reducing RV parking
  and addressing the restaurant issues. He suggested repaving and possibly including
  some angled parking.

  Public Works Commissioner Dittrich stated the roll-up boardwalk displayed by
  Public Works Commissioner Merrick was too narrow for use by the road. He stated
  the public did not want to see anything on the sand.

  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Stewart stated he supported repaving the
  road. He suggested recommending the Council approve repaving the roadway to
  the original asphalt and include a pedestrian walkway.

  Public Works Commissioner Merrick stated Option 2 did not seem to have much
  support.
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of February 23, 2022
Page 5 ofl2

  Public Safety Commissioner Spiegel stated he supported repairing the apron but
  not further than was ever in place. He stated the Sunset Restaurant issues were a
  nuisance. He suggested speaking to the County about relocating its cashier. He
  expressed opposition to walkways encroaching into the sand. He stated wave
  uprush studies were hit and miss at best.

  Vice Chair Major stated he did not want a mountainside walkway. He stated there
  would never be enough parking to accommodate the public, so it should not be the
  focus. He stated safety issues should be addressed with minimal construction. He
  supported rehabilitating broken asphalt. He stated the public safety problems were
  primarily on weekends with too many people and issues with the restaurant.

MOTION  Public Works Commissioner Dittrich moved, and Public Works Commission Chair
  Simmens seconded a motion to provide a recommendation to the City Council to
  approve repaving the existing road, including repair of the existing shoulder, not to
  extend beyond the City right-of-way.

  In response to Public Safety Commission Chair Frost, Public Works Director
  DuBoux stated use of funding should not impact the Commissioner’s
  recommendations. He stated the Council would make those decisions with input
  from staff.

  In response to Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Stewart, Public Works
  Director DuBoux stated the existing edge of pavement could be misleading in some
  of the photographs.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Stewart suggested changing “not to extend
  beyond the City right-of-way” to “extending up to 11 feet from the existing edge
  line of the travel lane.”

  In response to Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major, Public Works Director
  DuBoux stated there was no documented history of the original construction. In
  response to Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major, Public Works Director
  DuBoux stated the project could include measures to protect further degradation of
  the roadway.

  The Friendly Amendment was accepted by the maker and seconder.

  Public Works Commissioner Merrick stated he preferred to see the edge set back
  for a potential future boardwalk or walkway. He stated the shoulder was lower
  because it was never repaired in previous repaving projects.
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of February 23, 2022
Page 6 of 12

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Public Works Commissioner Merrick suggested replacing “extending up to 11 feet
  from the existing edge line of the travel lane” with “to incorporate the landside of
  the road to the fullest extent available without retaining walls and on the beach side
  the edge of payment should not exceed eight feet from the City right-of-way.” The
  amendment was accepted by the maker and seconder.

  The question was called, and the amended motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Public Works Commission Chair Simmens moved to include angled parking on the
  beach side at an angle no greater than 45 degrees.

  Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs asked how many parking spots were gained if
  all landside parking was changed to angled parking. Public Works Director
  DuBoux stated 45-degree angled parking would provide 29 to 30 additional spots
  on the beach side. He stated parking width would increase making it unfeasible for
  the land side.

  The motion died due to lack of a second.

MOTION  Public Works Commission Chair Simmens moved, and Public Works
  Commissioner Dittrich seconded a motion to include in the recommendation to the
  City Council that it approve the inclusion of bicycle “share the road” designation
  in the roadway. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs suggested discussing with B&H removing the
  gate guard to reduce traffic backups. Public Works Director DuBoux stated the City
  had a good working relationship with B&H and would bring that up.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost suggested asking B&H to add staffing in the
  lot to communicate with staff at the kiosk regarding parking space availability.

  In response to Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs, Public Works Director DuBoux
  stated he would discuss with Code Enforcement how to correct the problems
  created by Sunset Restaurant. Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs suggested putting
  a time limit on the first five parking spots.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost stated opening the restaurant’s back gate to
  allow parking in the restaurant parking lot would reduce backups in the roadway.

MOTION  Public Works Commissioner Dittrich moved and Public Works Commission Vice
  Chair Major seconded a motion to provide a recommendation to the City Council
  to add delineated parking spots.

  Public Works Commissioner Merrick expressed support for delineated parking
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of February 23, 2022
Page 7 of 12

  spots. He stated the community would not support pay stations.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost agreed delineated parking spots would
  prevent RVs from parking there.

  Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs asked if delineated spots were only to prevent
  RVs. He suggested oversized vehicles prohibited signage would suffice.

  Public Works Commissioner Dittrich stated that was only part of the problem. He
  stated the restaurant workers and restaurant scooters were taking up parking spots.

  Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs stated delineated spots often result in losing
  parking spaces.

  The question was called and the motion carried 9-1, Public Safety Commissioner
  Gibbs dissenting.

MOTION  Public Works Commissioner Dittrich moved to provide a recommendation to the
  City Council to include installation of paid parking on weekends.

  The motion died due to lack of a second.

MOTION  Public Works Commissioner Dittrich moved, and Public Works Commissioner
  Merrick seconded a motion to provide a recommendation to the City Council to
  include a biodegradable, roll-up walkway on the beach side not to exceed five feet
  in width.

  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Stewart stated similar walkways in Florida
  and Catalina Island required constant maintenance and would not be practical.

  Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major suggested that type of walkway be
  considered in the future after initial work was completed to see if it was still needed.

  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Stewart agreed with Public Works
  Commission Vice Chair Major.

  Public Works Commissioner Merrick and Public Safety Commission Chair Frost
  agreed with waiting to see if the proposed work would resolve pedestrian concerns.

  Public Safety Commissioner Anneet stated there were ecological risks with using
  wood on the beach. She agreed with taking a slower approach.

  Public Works Commissioner Dittrich withdrew the motion.
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of February 23, 2022

MOTION  Public Works Commissioner Dittrich moved, and Public Safety Commissioner
  Gibbs seconded a motion to provide a recommendation to the City Council to install
  speed humps on the road when the repaving was done.

  Vice Chair Major suggested considering rough road bumps as an alternative.

  Public Works Commission Chair Simmens stated speed humps were more visible
  and motorists could prepare to slow down.

  In response to Public Works Director DuBoux, Public Works Commissioner
  Dittrich stated the speed humps could be installed from PCH to Birdview Ave.

  Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs suggested starting afier the intersection to the
  creek near the Point Dume Club.

  In response to Public Works Commissioner Merrick, Public Works Director
  DuBoux discussed warrants required to install a stop sign.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated speed humps could not be installed on a
  curve. He stated only one could be installed between PCH and Zuma Bay Way.

  Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major stated he would want more public
  input before recommending anything beyond the area just coming off PCH.

FRIENDLY AMEWNDMENT
  Public Works Commission Chair Simmens suggested adding “along Westward
  Beach Road in conformance with the City’s Public Works Speed Hump Policy.”

  The Friendly Amendment was accepted by the maker and seconder.

  The question was called and the amended motion carried unanimously.

  In response to Public Works Commissioner Merrick, Public Works Director
  DuBoux stated he would present the Commissions’ recommendations to the City
  Council and, if approved, staff would proceed with design, which would be brought
  back to the Commissions for review.

  Public Works Commissioner Merrick expressed concern about the loss of funding
  due to what was not being addressed in those recommendations. In response to
  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Stewart, Public Works Director DuBoux
  estimated that funding was approximately $150,000 for project design. He stated
  he would discuss options with Metro.
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of February 23, 2022
Page9ofl2

MOVED  Public Works Commissioner Merrick moved to request that the City Council
  provide the Public Works Commission, Public Safety Commission, and staff with
  direction on additional components for pedestrian, bicycle, and emergency vehicle
  access on Westward Beach.

  Public Works Commissioner Merrick withdrew his motion.

MOTION  Public Works Commissioner Merrick moved, and Chair Simmens seconded a
  motion to provide a recommendation to the City Council to include a boardwalk or
  elevated boardwalk made of environmentally-friendly material for pedestrian
  traffic on the beach side of Westward Beach Road within the City right-of-way.

  Public Safety Commissioner Anneet asked if this boardwalk would be included in
  the eight-foot setback.

  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Stewart suggested requesting a pedestrian
  walkway be brought back for further review of design and how it would be used.

  Public Works Commissioner Dittrich agreed with Public Safety Commission Vice
  Chair Stewart. He suggested tabling the discussion to a future meeting.

  The question was called, and the motion was carried unanimously by the Public
  Works Commission, and failed 1-4 by the Public Safety Commission, Public Safety
  Commissioner Spiegel, Public Safety Commissioner Anneet, Public Safety
  Commission Vice Chair Stewart, and Public Safety Commissioner Gibbs
  dissenting.

MOTION  Public Works Commission Chair Simmens moved to j3rovide a recommendation to
  the City Council to give further direction to the Commission as to whether it wants
  the Commissions to pursue a pedestrian walkway.

  The motion died due to lack of a second.

MOTION  Public Safety Commissioner Anneet moved, and Public Works Commission Chair
  Simmens seconded a motion to include in the recommendation to City Council that
  the project be brought back to the Public Works Commission and Public Safety
  Commission approximately eight months to one year following completion of the
  project construction for evaluation of whether additional work to improve public
  safety and emergency access along Westward Beach Road should be considered.
  The question was called, and the motion carried 9-0, Public Works Commissioner
  Dittrich absent.

  B.  Los Angeles County Measure R and M Transportation Funding Projects (continued
  from January 20, 2022)
  Recommended Action: 1) Identif~,r projects to improve safety on Pacific Coast
  Highway and canyon roads using Los Angeles County Measure R and Measure M
  transportation funds; and 2) Provide a recommendation to City Council.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the report. He discussed priority projects,
  including some, such as the undergrounding of utilities along PCH, that would be
  applicable for funding through the recently approved federal infrastructure bill.

  Ryan Embree suggested the Commissions request clarity on what Measure R funds
  could be used for Malibu Canyon Road. He suggested State funding should be
  provided for projects under Caltrans jurisdiction. He discussed the need for a
  pedestrian undercrossing at Malibu Seafood and a right turn lane into Paradise
  Cove. He suggested the City urge Caltrans to provide funding for needed projects
  on its State highway. He suggested using Measure M funds for City roads.

  Hans Laetz requested Morning View Drive be repaired. He discussed damage from
  truck traffic. He discussed safety improvements needed on Guernsey Avenue.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost stated Morning View Drive was included in
  next year’s pavement plan.

  Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major thanked the speakers. He agreed with
  Mr. Embree about work that should be funded by Caltrans. He asked if the City
  could negotiate the ownership of utility lines with SCE if the City used its funds to
  underground the lines. Public Works Director DuBoux stated SCE would still own
  the lines. He discussed the Public Utility Commission (PUC) involvement in
  change of ownership of lines. Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major
  discussed latitude the City would have if it owned the lines and leased them to SCE.

MOTION  Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major moved to recommend to the City
  Council that the City’s use of its funding for undergrounding of utilities be
  contingent upon what the City would receive from SCE in exchange.

  The motion died due to lack of a second.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated Measure R and Measure M funds could only
  be used for projects on PCH, Malibu Canyon Road, and Kanan Dume Road.

  Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major expressed support for pedestrian
  enhancements near Moonshadows and Malibu Seafood. He requested further
  discussion of median improvements between Trancas Canyon and Broad Beach.
  He agreed with Mr. Laetz about degraded conditions on Morning View Drive and
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission

  Guernsey Avenue and that repairs to those roads should be a priority.

  Mr. Laetz suggested considering equity between eastern and western Malibu. He
  stated the median population center of Malibu was Paradise Cove, yet most funds
  were used in eastern Malibu. He stated the only priority project in western Malibu
  was a median on PCH west of Trancas Canyon Road.

  Public Safety Commission Vice Chair Stewart commended Public Works Director
  DuBoux for working on using federal infrastructure funding for the City’s projects.
  He discussed the undercrossing by Malibu Seafood. In response to Public Safety
  Commission Vice Chair Stewart, Public Works Director DuBoux discussed
  Caltrans’ proposed pedestrian crossing project that had been abandoned. He stated
  the City and Caltrans continued to discuss options. Public Safety Commission Vice
  Chair Stewart stated the signal synchronization project needed to be extended west.
  He discussed other points in need of traffic signals for safe left turns between John
  Tyler Road and Paradise Cove.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost discussed the warrant process. He stated
  Latigo Canyon Road could qualif\j for a signal, but Winding Way was a private
  road and Puerco Canyon Road would be unlikely to meet warrants.

  Public Works Commission Chair Simmens discussed previous proposals from
  Caltrans for a crosswalk at the bottom of the hill by Malibu Seafood.

  Commissioner Anneet left the meeting at 7:17 p.m.

  In response to Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major, Public Works Director
  DuBoux confirmed Measure R and Measure M funding could not be used for
  Malibu Park road repairs. He confirmed Morning View Road was

  Public Safety Commissioner Anneet returned to the meeting at 7:50 p.m.

MOTION  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost moved, and Public Works Commission Vice
  Chair Major seconded a motion to recommend to the City Council that it direct staff
  to use the City’s allotted Measure R and Measure M transportation funds, as well
  as any available funding from the recently approved Federal Infrastructure Bill, for
  the priority projects identified by staff. The question was called, and the motion
  carried 9-0, Public Works Commissioner Dittrich absent.

MOTION  Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major moved to recommend to the City
  Council that any consideration of the use of Federal Infrastructure Funding for the
  undergrounding of utility lines include conversations with the owners of those lines
  regarding how the use of the City’s federal funds for the undergrounding will
 Malibu Public Works Commission and Public Safety Commission
Joint Special Meeting
Minutes of February 23, 2022
Page 12 of 12

  impact the ownership of those lines.

  Public Works Commission Chair Simmens and Public Safety Commission Chair
  Frost expressed concerns with trying to require SCE to enter into that type of
  discussion or negotiation.

  Public Works Commission Vice Chair Major withdrew the motion.

  Public Safety Commission Chair Frost thanked all the Commissioners and staff for
  their contributions to these discussions. He stated joint meetings between these two
  commissions were beneficial.

ADJOURNMENT

  At 8:09 p.m., Public Safety Commission Chair Frost adjourned the meeting.

  Approved and adopted by the Public Works Commission of the City
